title: A Short Story from My Past

opts: я (уже) делал — до момента в прошлом
prepTasks.correct: я (уже) делал — до момента в прошлом

writingModel: The Day I Almost Didn't Arrive — by Rustam Seilov

It was the first week of the new semester, and I had been looking forward to the first WKU volleyball practice of the year for a long time. I had been playing for the student team for almost a year by then, and I had trained hard all summer. The practice was at 5 p.m. on the other side of the city.

When I left the dormitory, I had checked the bus schedule carefully. The number 7 bus left at 4:15. I had ten minutes. I walked quickly to the stop — and as I arrived, I watched the bus pull away. The number 7 had come early. I had missed it by thirty seconds.

I stood at the stop and thought about my options. I had already missed the previous practice due to a lecture clash, so missing this one as well felt impossible. I decided to walk. The journey would take forty minutes. The practice started in forty-five. I was going to be late. I walked anyway.

What I hadn't known was that the route passed through the market district. As I walked, the street filled with noise and movement — sellers calling out, children running, the smell of bread from a bakery I hadn't noticed before. I had been so focused on the bus that I hadn't seen any of it. I started walking more slowly, looking around, forgetting briefly that I was almost certainly going to be late.

By the time I reached the sports hall, the practice had already started — five minutes earlier, not at 5 p.m. as I had thought. I had run the last three hundred metres. Zhibek was waiting outside. "Where were you?" she said. "I've been covering for you with the coach." I hadn't known she would do that. I hadn't asked.

That evening, I thought about the day. I had missed the bus, walked through a market I hadn't seen before, arrived five minutes late, and been helped by someone who hadn't needed to help me. It had all happened because the number 7 bus had come early. None of it would have happened otherwise. Sometimes, I think, the things that go wrong are the things that end up mattering.

writingTemplate.hint: Choose a title that suggests something unexpected or personal.

writingTemplate.placeholder: when + what you had been doing/expecting
writingTemplate.hint: Set the scene: when it was, and what had been happening before the main event.

writingTemplate.placeholder: arrived / got there / started — main past event
writingTemplate.hint: "When I arrived..." — the main past event. What happened?

writingTemplate.placeholder: what had happened earlier that made this worse
writingTemplate.hint: "I had already missed X, so..." — use Past Perfect for earlier context.

writingTemplate.placeholder: your decision in response to the problem
writingTemplate.hint: What did you decide to do? Simple past.
"What I hadn't known was..." = the unexpected element. Past Perfect negative.

writingTemplate.placeholder: arrived / finished / happened — by the time structure
writingTemplate.hint: "By the time I arrived, it had already..." — use the deadline structure.

writingTemplate.placeholder: what the day had taught you
writingTemplate.hint: Reflect on the experience. What did it mean? What had you learned?
